title: Lane Agent Registry Claim
description: One running lane's addressable identity, claimed at /begin-orchestration Step 4 and released at lane close. Exists because ListAgents returns auto-generated session nicknames that are unstable across restart and carry no repo, lane or roadmap — measured live 2026-08-21 (engine-rs-5b, mev-d8, agentic-portfolio-d9, base-template-b6, okf-core-d0, bastion-c4, 11 peers total) — so a lane cannot be addressed by role ('whoever is driving mev's autonomous-foundation lane') without a record like this. Sibling to lane.schema.json and block.schema.json. This block ships the shape, checker and read helpers only; writing claims is BT.6.E.

agent_name.description: The ListAgents nickname this agent is currently reachable at (e.g. 'base-template-b6'). Recorded here specifically because it is unstable across restart and carries no repo/lane/roadmap on its own — this record is what turns a volatile nickname into an addressable, restart-surviving identity for the lane.

repo.description: Repo slug this lane is driving, as registered in brain.toml. Lets a caller filter claims down to 'who is working in this repo right now'.

lane.description: The lane's name/slug, matching the <name> in its lane-<name>.json record (lane.schema.json). Lets a caller address 'whoever is driving lane X', independent of which agent nickname currently holds it.

roadmap.description: Slug of the owning roadmap directory this lane runs under. Disambiguates the same lane name reused across different roadmaps.

started_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with timezone marking when this agent claimed the lane. Fixed for the life of the claim; distinguishes 'how long has this lane been running' from heartbeat's 'is it still alive'.

heartbeat.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with timezone, updated periodically while the agent is alive. The staleness signal: a heartbeat older than the checker's threshold is how BT.6.D detects an abandoned lane versus a merely slow one, once joined against ListAgents liveness.
